subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated exec calls with identical arguments and the same structured nonzero outcome count as no progress even when their output text changes?
rationale: The patch correctly implements and proves that policy, but only maintainers can accept the resulting possibility that an intentional nonzero polling workflow is stopped after the configured threshold.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprint
options.body: Rebase and merge after an agent-runtime owner confirms the runaway-loop protection outweighs the bounded false-positive risk for repeated nonzero polling.

options.title: Narrow volatile-output normalization
options.body: Keep output partly significant and normalize only explicitly supported volatile tokens, reducing false positives but risking additional unrecognized loop variants.

recommendation.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprint
recommendation.body: Rebase and merge after an agent-runtime owner confirms the runaway-loop protection outweighs the bounded false-positive risk for repeated nonzero polling.

likelyOwner.reason: They identified the production result-contract gap and are the clearest recent reviewer connected to this exact loop-detection boundary.
